## Planned contrasts on E* (lower = learns sooner)

| ID | Hypothesis | X vs Y | Test | E* X | E* Y | A (X sooner) | p one-sided | p Holm | p two-sided (exploratory) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | H2: guide speeds up Rainbow | rainbow_g vs rainbow | unpaired | 100 120 120 100 80 | 220 220 220 220 220 | 1.0 | 0.004 | 0.016 | 0.0079 |
| C2 | H2: guide speeds up D3QN | d3qn_g vs d3qn | unpaired | 120 140 160 120 80 | 60 60 140 100 60 | 0.18 | 0.9683 | 1.0 | 0.127 |
| C3 | H1: DDQN at least as fast as DQN | ddqn vs dqn | paired | 80 60 100 80 100 | 100 80 120 140 100 | 0.8 | 0.0625 | 0.1875 | 0.125 |
| C4 | H3: guided Rainbow beats best unguided (d3qn) | rainbow_g vs d3qn | unpaired | 100 120 120 100 80 | 60 60 140 100 60 | 0.28 | 0.9048 | 1.0 | 0.2381 |

Exact tests: unpaired = all C(n,k) label splits on ranks (5 vs 5: min p = 1/252); paired = all 2^n sign flips of per-seed differences (5 pairs: min p = 1/32). One-sided direction = the hypothesis; Holm over the one-sided p's. Two-sided p is exploratory. Censored E* = never learned within the budget (ranked slowest). Test code written after training; contrasts and directions are the pre-stated ones.
